claims_supported: SBI Holdings says its U.S. subsidiary SBI Holdings USA will invest USD 100 million in Erebor Bank, N.A.
The Japanese announcement uses future-tense investment language; this record classifies the investment as announced/planned, not verified as closed or funded.
SBI describes Erebor as a U.S. digital bank supporting blockchain-based payments and stablecoin deposits and withdrawals.
SBI says the group has investments in Ripple Labs and Circle, handles USDC and RLUSD in Japan, and is developing JPYSC with Startale.
limitations: The announcement does not establish that the USD 100 million investment has closed or been funded.
The release does not disclose the investment's ownership percentage, governance rights or detailed conditions.
The USD 7 billion-plus Erebor deposit figure is an SBI-reported figure in this release, not an independently retrieved Call Report in this artifact.
No raw response bytes or SHA-256 receipt were captured.

source_registry.authority: primary regulator deposit-insurance approval and institution status
claims_supported: FDIC approved Erebor Bank's deposit-insurance application on 2025-12-16, subject to conditions.
The FDIC approval required a minimum 12% Tier 1 leverage ratio during the first three years and capital-call arrangements if the bank fell below specified capital requirements.
The FDIC's institution table lists Erebor Bank, N.A. certificate 59378 with date opened 2026-02-06.
limitations: Deposit-insurance approval and bank opening do not establish SBI's planned equity investment closing.
The capital and deposit figures reported by SBI were not independently reconciled to the latest bank Call Report here.

source_registry.publisher: SBI Holdings, SBI Shinsei Bank, SBI Shinsei Trust Bank, SBI VC Trade and Startale Group
claims_supported: SBI Shinsei Trust Bank is the issuer of JPYSC; SBI VC Trade is responsible for distribution and issuance-related business; Startale Group is the technology co-development partner.
Initial JPYSC distribution began within SBI VC Trade accounts; the release said public-chain circulation would follow after legal and tax matters were clarified.
The JPYSC launch was described as a trust-based Type 3 electronic payment instrument under Japanese law.
limitations: The source does not identify XRP as the settlement or collateral asset.
The initial account-limited launch is not proof of public-chain circulation.

source_registry.publisher: SBI Shinsei Trust Bank and SBI VC Trade
claims_supported: As of 2026-09-07, JPYSC issuance balance was reported at approximately JPY 20.1 billion.
SBI Shinsei Trust Bank began investing JPY 1.0 billion of JPYSC trust backing assets in short-term Japanese government bonds under the revised Japanese legal framework.
SBI VC Trade reported JPYSC Lending applications of approximately JPY 6.9 billion at that date.
limitations: These are issuer/operator disclosures, not independent reserve attestations.
The figures are a dated September 7 snapshot and must not be mixed with November 2 handling/lending balances.

claims_supported: SBI Holdings and Startale Group signed a basic agreement with BlackRock entities to explore a digital-asset ecosystem using tokenized money-market funds and JPYSC.
limitations: The source describes a basic agreement, not a launched product, completed investment or live settlement flow.
No XRP use or XRP collateral role is established.

source_registry.authority: official corporate membership and interoperability announcement
claims_supported: SBI Holdings and Startale joined Open Standard, which SBI says has more than 140 participating companies including Visa, Stripe, Mastercard, BlackRock and Coinbase.
SBI and Startale said they would explore a proof of concept for interoperability between JPYSC and Open USD (OUSD).
limitations: Coinbase's participation in Open Standard does not establish a direct bilateral agreement, equity relationship or operational integration between SBI and Coinbase.
The JPYSC/OUSD work is described as a proposed proof of concept, not a live payment route.

claims_supported: SBI says a consolidated subsidiary participated in Circle's ARC token presale consortium.
SBI describes the overall consortium raise as USD 222 million; SBI's own contribution amount is not disclosed.
SBI reiterates the SBI Circle Holdings joint venture, USDC distribution and the group's USD 50 million strategic Circle share investment.
limitations: Do not attribute the entire USD 222 million consortium raise to SBI.
ARC is Circle's network token, not XRP; no XRP purchase or demand is established.

competing_hypotheses.statement: SBI's Ripple equity stake, SBI Ripple Asia joint venture and SBI Remit XRP bridge corridors may create durable institutional XRP usage.
evidence_for: Existing relationship map records SBI's approximately 9% Ripple stake as of the 2025 investor presentation, 60% voting control of SBI Ripple Asia as of 2026-03-31, and XRP bridge remittances at the 2023 corridor launch.
evidence_against: No current SBI Remit XRP volume, average XRP inventory, settlement share or net purchase amount is disclosed in the sources reviewed.

competing_hypotheses.statement: SBI's growing JPYSC, USDC, RLUSD, OUSD interoperability and bank/payment investments may route some settlement and liquidity demand through stablecoins rather than XRP.
evidence_for: JPYSC service balances above JPY 30B and lending balances above JPY 10B; active USDC and RLUSD distribution; JPYSC/BlackRock and JPYSC/OUSD initiatives; planned Erebor investment.
evidence_against: Stablecoins may complement XRP in corridors where XRP provides an intermediate bridge or liquidity function; no measured corridor-level substitution is available.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Institutional projects using XRPL increase demand for the native XRP asset.
evidence_for: SBI Ripple Asia's tokenized-deposit proof of concept uses XRPL.
evidence_against: Tokenized deposits and deposit-backed digital money can be represented on XRPL without establishing material XRP holdings, collateral or bridge use.

disconfirming_evidence: SBI's JPYSC balances are issuer-reported service balances, not independently measured public-chain supply.
JPYSC was initially distributed within VCTRADE accounts, with public-chain circulation conditional on legal and tax matters.
JPYSC backing disclosed in September 2026 included Japanese government bonds, not XRP.
SBI's USD 100 million Erebor investment is announced as a future investment; closing and funding are not verified.
SBI's BlackRock and Open Standard relationships are agreements/proposed proof-of-concepts, not evidence of live XRP settlement.
SBI's Circle ARC presale contribution amount is not disclosed; the consortium's USD 222 million total must not be attributed to SBI.
